brief: NDX is up 7% since the bank's Sep 10 call and has broken above resistance, ending a May consolidation that had built intensifying bearish psychology. BTIG's SOX-vs-2000 analog counters: semis now sit near the March 2000 peak, implying this could be later-cycle than it looks, though the analog points to choppy consolidation, not an immediate crash. Carlyle argues AI's funding regime is shifting: cash flow no longer covers intended capex, so over 80% of AI capex through 2030 needs external financing, with AI financing seen exceeding $500bn in 2026. Hyperscaler net savings are down 86% as hyperscalers flip from liquidity providers to users, pushing AI from an earnings story toward a capital-markets one. Goldman ties this to concentration: its S&P ex-AI basket fell from roughly 3,300 to 3,075 since August even as SPX holds near 7,700; hedge funds bought TMT in September while selling other sectors, and the top 10 stocks are expected to drive over two-thirds of this quarter's earnings growth. Bond vol keeps rising despite a flat 10-year, risking a reversal if rates fall. Brazil's high real carry (Selic 13.75%, inflation 4.2-4.5%) cushions its election trade; JPM has Brazil at 8.9x forward earnings versus a possible 10.9x-13x rerating.
